analysis.title: JPMorgan Chase & Co. Jamie Dimon Unplugged
key_insights: BofA reiterates JPM as Top Idea with a Buy rating and $400 price objective (stock at $320.22), citing embedded optionality: share gains in deposits, investment banking, payments and wealth management, plus relative defensibility in a weaker macro backdrop.
Valuation: JPM trades at 12.7x 2027E P/E versus 11.0x for the peer median and 21.0x for the S&P 500, and at 2.5x YE27E P/TBV against BofA's 21% 2027E ROTCE forecast.
BofA argues the period when a rising tide lifted all banks may be nearing an end. As conditions become less forgiving, JPM's execution, risk management and balance sheet should matter more.

Capital: JPM carries a 14.0% standardized CET1 ratio and a 250bp buffer over its requirement in 3Q26, against 150bp for peers. Its SLR buffer is 125bp versus a 135bp peer average. JPM generated a 20% ROTCE in 3Q26.

Basel Endgame: JPM estimates the combined Basel III and GSIB re-proposals would raise required CET1 by about 4% versus the 2028 baseline. BofA expects the rules to be finalized by mid-December with limited changes from the March re-proposals.

Investment banking: Dimon called the environment trench warfare. JPM ranks #1 in global IB fees with 9.2% wallet share YTD (8.5% last year) and 9.8% global M&A share (8.0%). 3Q26 IB fees grew 14% y/y, with advisory fees up 32%.

Consumer: JPM ended 3Q26 with 5,164 branches (+3% y/y), added over 650,000 net new checking accounts in the quarter and holds 11.7% national deposit share (-10bp y/y). CCB client investment assets reached $1.42tn (+15% y/y).

Self-Directed Investing: Dimon acknowledged it is not yet on the level of Schwab or E*TRADE. Gaps include fractional shares and crypto trading. BofA sees checking and direct investing accounts becoming fungible.
Chase UK/Europe (launched in Germany in May 2026) is delivering retail deposits and reducing reliance on wholesale funding. BofA sees potential to eventually compete with Revolut.

AI: JPM has 50-100 significant use cases. BofA sees a revenue opportunity in Chase offering trusted agents to customers. Near-term AI savings are not expected to cut headcount, as Dimon would use the capacity to clear the product backlog. Firmwide technology expense rose 17% y/y in 3Q26.

Deposit economics: Dimon acknowledged AI tools may reduce 'lazy cash'. BofA expects banks to shift toward charging for services, and sees a full-product bank as better placed than a monoline deposit gatherer. CCB deposit margin was 2.78% in 3Q26, roughly flat y/y.

Cyber: AI has helped JPM find many more vulnerabilities than it knew of. Risk is industry-wide across vendors, clearing infrastructure and open-source code, and JPM's interconnectedness means it cannot fully insulate itself from failures elsewhere. Dimon pointed to FS-ISAC for threat-intelligence sharing.

Credit: BofA considers credit largely normalized, with card net charge-offs tracking about 3.2% for FY26. Dimon flagged complacency on rates and credit spreads, citing deficits, immigration, remilitarization and healthcare costs as inflationary pressures. The market prices three hikes through YE27, and a doubling of credit spreads is not far-fetched if the Fed must move more and faster.

Dimon sees AI capex financing risk as greater than the market appreciates and is willing to cede share, since assets could be bought at a discount if pricing breaks. BofA notes private credit and CRE refinancing assumptions are the risk if rates stay higher for longer.

Liquidity rule: a Fed rule giving credit for discount window access remains possible. Dimon's shareholder letter estimated this alone would add almost $500bn to JPM's lendable liquidity. The Fed's September 2026 final rules on stress-test transparency and SCB averaging are seen as a step in the right direction.

Succession: BofA calls CEO succession the most important long-term idiosyncratic risk. It sees a transition as a 2029 event at the earliest and expects the Street will need time to gain confidence in the next CEO.

CFO transition: CFO Jeremy Barnum will step down after six years. Bregje de Best, currently CFO of the Commercial & Investment Bank, succeeds him after 1Q27 results. Barnum becomes Vice Chairman and stays through early 2028.

Estimates: BofA 2026E/2027E/2028E EPS is $23.50/$25.50/$27.22, against Bloomberg consensus of $24.33/$25.55/$27.39. 2026E EPS growth is 16.5%, 2027E is 8.5%. 4Q26E quarterly EPS is $5.66 after $5.75 in 3Q26 (actual).

market_movers.rationale: Top Idea. Embedded optionality, share gains and balance-sheet strength should let the stock outperform across economic scenarios.

sector_views.rationale: JPM is favored as conditions become less forgiving, while BofA expects peer profitability to be challenged by worsening credit or a sharp drop in asset prices.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM's execution, capital buffer (250bp over requirement versus 150bp for peers) and risk management should let it outperform in multiple scenarios, at 12.7x 2027E P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: A shifting macro, such as worsening credit or a sharp drop in asset prices, could challenge JPM's profitability. Dimon warns a doubling of credit spreads is plausible if the Fed must hike faster than the three hikes priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rise in the probability of worsening credit quality from current benign levels, or the Fed being forced to move more and faster than the three hikes priced through YE27.
